steps.do: Prerequisite — this loop remediates things that already exist. Before starting, build and run the Support Triage Copilot from cookbook 07 so you have a real workflow with recent runs. You will need three real ids from it: a few flagged trace ids, the workflow_id, and an agent_id bound in that workflow. Aria does not create the subject workflow or its traces.
steps.see: An existing workflow (from SCN-07) listed under Workflows, with recent runs you can open.

steps.do: Collect the flagged trace ids you will enqueue. In the sidebar, under Operate, click Observability, stay on the Traces tab, and set the Filter by status dropdown to Error to surface the weak runs. Click each weak trace to open it on the right — its full trace_id appears in the page URL (?trace=…) and you can also paste an id into the Search traces box to confirm it. Note 2-3 trace ids — you will paste them later.
fill: Error (the option values are All statuses / OK / Error / In progress)
2-3 trace_id values from the weak runs (from the URL after selecting each trace)
steps.see: A filtered list of trace rows (each showing the trace name + an ERROR status badge). Selecting a row opens its detail and puts the full trace_id in the URL — keep those ids handy for the enqueue step.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › New goal
steps.do: In the sidebar, under Integrations and preview (the page carries a Preview badge), click Plans. Type Aria's one-line intent into the Goal box, verbatim — the phrase review queue proposes both queue steps and the word workflow (calibration) proposes the calibrate step. Set Autonomy to Stop before each change (the ask_each level).
fill: Our workflow's recent runs look weak — set up a review queue for the flagged traces and kick off a workflow calibration. (canonical intent — copy from intent.md)
Stop before each change (= ask_each)
steps.see: The button shows Decomposing…, then Aria opens the plan's detail page. Breadcrumb Plans › PLAN-…, status badge DRAFT.

steps.do: Confirm Aria decomposed the sentence into the three remediation steps. Note the third step, workflow.calibrate, is Aria's first async capability. Compare against expected-plan.json.
fill: workflow.calibrate — tier mutate, ASYNC (needs EXISTING workflow_id + agent_id)
steps.see: A three-row Plan steps list (review_queue.create, review_queue.add_items, workflow.calibrate), each with a PENDING badge.

steps.do: Approve the plan shape. Click Approve plan in the top-right of the plan header.
steps.see: The status badge flips from DRAFT to APPROVED, and an Execute button appears.

steps.do: Start running the plan. Click Execute. Aria reaches the first step, review_queue.create, but the planner could not know your queue's name or question schema, so it pauses on a violet Aria needs information form with two buttons, Continue plan and Skip step. Each of the three steps works the same way: an input form for the fields the planner could not fill, then (under ask_each) an Approve / Deny prompt.
steps.see: The review_queue.create row shows WAITING INPUT and an Aria needs information form is open above the step list.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › PLAN-… (input form)
steps.do: Fill the review-queue form from triage-review.queue.json: the name, a description, and the four-question questions JSON array (the form rejects invalid JSON). Note two special types: failure_mode is categorical (with options) and expected_answer uses target expectation (its answer becomes ground truth on the trace). Click Continue plan, then Approve.
fill: Human triage of weak workflow runs: was the resolution correct, what failed, how severe, and what the answer should have been.

[{"key": "resolution_correct", "title": "Did the workflow reach the correct resolution?", "type": "pass_fail", "required": true, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "failure_mode", "title": "Primary failure mode", "type": "categorical", "options": ["wrong_tool", "missing_evidence", "hallucinated_claim", "bad_escalation", "none"], "required": true, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "severity", "title": "Severity (1-5)", "type": "numeric", "required": false, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "expected_answer", "title": "What should the answer have been? (becomes the expectation)", "type": "text", "required": false, "target": "expectation"}]
steps.see: After Approve, review_queue.create shows DONE and the plan pauses on the review_queue.add_items form.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › PLAN-… (input form)
steps.do: Enqueue the real flagged traces (the review_queue.add_items step). The planner linked this step's queue_id to the queue just created, so the form asks only for trace ids (a JSON array; optional experiment id and assignee). Enter the real trace ids you noted from Observability — replace the placeholders in enqueue.json — click Continue plan, then Approve.
fill: ["tr-…", "tr-…", "tr-…"] (the REAL flagged trace ids from Observability — not placeholders)
steps.see: After Approve, review_queue.add_items shows DONE and the plan pauses on the workflow.calibrate form.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › PLAN-… (input form)
steps.do: Kick off the workflow calibration (the workflow.calibrate step). Enter the real workflow_id and agent_id from calibrate.json (the SCN-07 workflow and the agent bound in it), click Continue plan, then Approve. Approving enqueues a real workflow-calibration (refinement) job; the step parks in WAITING JOB and the plan stays RUNNING — it does not pause for a human.
fill: the REAL existing workflow id (the SCN-07 workflow)
the REAL agent id bound in that workflow
steps.see: After Approve, the workflow.calibrate row shows WAITING JOB and the plan status is RUNNING. A new entry also appears under the workflow's Calibration runs — the real async refinement job.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › PLAN-… (waiting on a job)
steps.do: Let the async job run. This is the genuinely asynchronous part of the loop and there is nothing to click: the plan worker polls the job about every 10 seconds and resumes the plan by itself. Refresh the plan page (the Plans UI has no Poll button) until the step leaves WAITING JOB. The job counts as done when it reaches candidate_ready (or applied); rejected, failed or error fails the step and the plan. The plan does not apply the candidate. (Over the API, POST /aria/plans/{id}/poll advances it on demand.) With the default fake evaluator the job's scores are canned.
steps.see: The workflow.calibrate row flips to DONE and the plan reaches COMPLETED with all three steps done.
steps.asset: Plan resumed and completed after the async job

steps.where: Operate › Review Queues  +  Also in the alpha › Workflows
steps.do: Final verification across surfaces. Review Queues › weak-runs-triage shows the flagged traces enqueued and ready to review. Workflows › (your workflow) › Calibration runs shows the calibration job at candidate ready (or applied). The Aria plan (under Plans, status COMPLETED, all three steps done) is the orchestration record for the whole triage → remediation loop.
steps.see: A populated weak-runs-triage queue, a finished calibration run on the workflow, and a completed Aria plan — the governance → remediation loop end to end.

steps.do: (Optional follow-up) Have reviewers answer the queue's questions — the expectation-targeted expected_answer writes ground truth back onto each trace. Then compare the recalibrated workflow against its baseline runs and feed the hard cases into its eval dataset (see SCN-01 / SCN-10) to keep tightening the loop.
steps.see: Submitted reviews write assessments + expectations back onto the traces, giving you ground-truth labels to compare the recalibrated workflow against its baseline.
